narrative:
The model estimates an 81% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your profile that historically align with employees who eventually depart.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outlook, in order of importance, were the availability of other job opportunities, your overall years of experience, and your monthly salary level. Having received other job offers while employed here was the single biggest driver pushing the prediction toward leaving; most employees the model expects to stay have not received such external offers. Your six to ten years of total professional experience also pulled the prediction toward departure. While this is a solid amount of experience, it is more common among those who leave than among the larger group the model predicts will remain, who are mostly in the one-to-five-year range. Finally, your salary in the 11k–15k SAR bracket contributed further toward the leave prediction. Although this is above average, the model associates this specific pay band more with employees who ultimately move on than with those who stay.

Taken together, these signals led the system to conclude you are likely to leave. The organization should discuss retention measures with you, such as clearer career progression or adjusted compensation, while you may wish to reflect on whether your external opportunities better match your long-term goals.
